boundary: This ledger records LINKAGE, not coverage. A status says which shipped mechanical controls cite a rule, and each control carries a residue naming what it does not catch; the residue is the honest half of every claim. None of the statuses means a rule is enforced: gate-linked means at least one deterministic repository gate cites the rule, hook-linked means at least one runtime hook cites it and no gate does, prose-only means no shipped control cites it and the rule binds through the governing prose alone. Nothing in this file is a completeness or coverage measure, and deriving a score from it misreads it.

hooks.residue: Covers the file_path argument of Read, Write, and Edit (absolute by tool contract, so the relative-to-a-named-root carve-out never applies there) and the optional search-root path of Glob (which should be absolute). Honours the carve-out: a Glob pattern is legitimately relative to its named root and is never judged, and a Glob call with no path (the current directory as the named root) is allowed. Does not judge paths inside Bash command text, other path-bearing tools or parameters, or whether an absolute path points at the intended target.

A best-effort QUOTE-AWARE LEXICAL check over the Bash command string (the shipped shlex segmentation): it judges git push and git commit segments only - the LITERAL commit subcommand; a merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, or rebase that also lands commits on the protected line is out of scope by design, because the accidental case this layer guards is the direct git commit and server-side branch protection remains the real gate. The push layer parses options with a value-skip for the separated value-taking options (--push-option/-o, --repo, --receive-pack/--exec, and --recurse-submodules, whose value is MANDATORY and hence separable - verified against git 2.53.0, which consumes the next token as the value and rejects a bare form) and a --/--end-of-options boundary. Force, delete, sweep, and prune flags are detected VALUE-AWARE inside the token loop, so an option value is never read as a flag (git push -o --force origin main carries a push-option VALUE, not a force flag): every force spelling counts (-f/--force clustered or long, any --force-with-lease spelling - a lease-guarded force still rewrites the remote ref - --force-if-includes, and --mirror, which implies force), plus the ref-sweeping modes: --mirror, a forced --all/--branches, the MATCHING refspec (a bare : pushes every branch existing on both ends and +: is its forced form; either ASKS, a matching-refspec push this guard cannot prove misses the protected branches), and --prune combined with a wildcard or matching refspec (which DELETES every remote branch absent locally with NO force flag - witnessed deleting a remote master - so it ASKS; a --prune whose refspec mapping comes only from configuration falls under the configuration residual below). Operand ROLES follow the grammar git itself uses (git push <repository> <refspec>...): the FIRST bare operand is the repository and is never judged as a destination (a remote literally named main is not a false deny), and only the later, refspec-position operands are judged, by exact case-sensitive DESTINATION name (tolerant of a refs/heads/ or heads/ prefix); a skip-set omission can only shift operands toward over-inclusion, never move a real refspec into the exempt repository slot. A protected DELETION is denied like a force: a --delete or clustered -d flag whose refspec-position operand names a protected branch, and the empty-source :<dst> delete refspec (:main); the deny banner names the actual act, force-push vs branch deletion. When no refspec names a destination (a refspec-less force-push) or the refspec is HEAD/@, the SESSION-CWD current branch is read by a scrubbed read-only symbolic-ref probe (every ambient GIT_* removed, offline, 5s timeout), and a detached or unreadable HEAD reads as UNKNOWN, never as not-protected. Git resolves a pushed or FORCED HEAD/@ to the current branch; a DELETED HEAD or :@ git itself REJECTS as a nonexistent or invalid remote ref, so the probe-backed deny on a deleted HEAD/@ is a harmless safe-direction over-deny kept for uniformity, not a claim that git resolves a deleted HEAD to the current branch. It does NOT catch: a push or commit outside the Bash tool; a git alias or shell function that renames git or expands to a push; a destination supplied by SHELL EXPANSION rather than a literal token (git push --force origin "$BRANCH" with BRANCH holding a protected name, a command substitution, or a glob): a lexical guard judges the literal token and cannot resolve runtime shell state - the same inherent boundary git_discard discloses for its variable and substitution forms; a FRAGMENTED command word or verb (shell quoting that splits the git command word or the push/commit verb so neither the parsed segments nor the raw scan sees a contiguous git-plus-verb keyword; a plain command-word wrapper such as env/sudo/command/xargs IS caught by the raw scan and ASKS); a WRAPPED push in a compound in which ANY other segment, EARLIER OR LATER, parses with git as its command word (git status && sudo git push --force origin main, and equally env git push --force origin main && git status): the benign git segment satisfies the saw-git check, so the wrapped-catch raw scan never runs and the wrapped force-push is silently allowed - an adversarial best-effort residual of the same class as the fragmented command word, disclosed and not chased; a destination supplied by CONFIGURATION rather than the command line (push.default, branch.<name>.pushRemote/merge, remote.<name>.push refspecs, a triangular-push setup), so the bare-push HEAD proxy can diverge from the configured upstream mapping; a protected line under a NON-DEFAULT name (the set ships as main/master); or a rewrite landed on the remote side or by a hosting-provider action (a protected-NAMED force-push or deletion is denied redirect-independently, and a current-branch force-push or deletion under an unresolvable -C/--git-dir/GIT_* redirect ASKS, so none silent-allows). SAFE-DIRECTION OVER-DENIES, accepted and disclosed (re-issue without the contrived flag combination): negation and no-op flags are not modelled, so a --force or --delete cancelled by a later --no-force/--no-delete still denies, --force-if-includes ALONE (a documented no-op without --force-with-lease) denies, and a --dry-run push carrying any force or delete spelling is judged like the real thing and denies. On a shell parse error, OR when a command-word wrapper hides git so no parsed segment resolves to git, it falls back to a conservative raw scan that ASKS (never a hard deny, never a silent allow) on an apparent git force-push (any -f/--force/--for-prefix/--mirror/--all form, or a +refspec anchored to start, whitespace, or either quote character, so a quoted "+main:main" under sudo is caught), an apparent branch deletion (a --de-prefix long flag, or a d carried ANYWHERE in a short - cluster, mirroring the force cluster shape so a wrapped -dv is caught, name-independent like the force spellings; or an empty-source :<protected-name> refspec, judged by its visible name), or an apparent git commit. The raw scan OVER-MATCHES by design (a case-different name, an attached -o value ending in f, an unrelated + or -d token, or prose mentioning the keywords ASKS), so re-issue a wrongly-flagged command as a plain, parseable git command. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the accidental case, not an adversary determined to evade it.

gates.residue: Total over the surface it examines: an OPEN merge_pending row carrying a TYPED ref (pr:N, decision:X) whose merge or record evidence exists in the declared truth sources always fails the gate. It reads only typed structured refs; a narrative number in prose, an untyped row, or a register kept outside the declared surface is out of scope by design (D9), and drift the truth sources themselves cannot see (an unpushed local merge, a PR merged under a subject with no (#N) marker) passes. In a checkout with no orchestration registry the live leg is NOT APPLICABLE (the record is machine-local by design) and the self-test carries the assurance; that scope boundary is printed, never silent.

hooks.residue: A best-effort QUOTE-AWARE LEXICAL check over the Bash command string: tokenized with a shell lexer (shlex, posix, punctuation-aware) that respects quotes and grouped into segments on the unquoted shell operators ; | || && & ( ) and newlines, so a subshell-grouped commit (( git commit --author=... )) is judged too, and a trailer hiding inside a quoted -m message (-m "fix; Co-authored-by: Claude", which the old whitespace split broke at the ;) now lives intact in the single message token and is caught by a substring scan on that token. On a git commit-family segment (commit, merge, cherry-pick, am, rebase, revert, commit-tree) it flags a Co-Authored-By trailer inside any token or an --author value (--author=X or --author X) naming an AI; in ANY segment it flags a git-identity env var (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME) or a user.name/user.email value (a -c user.name=X inline or a config user.name X pair) naming an AI, so setting the identity in a prior segment then committing is caught. git global options that take an argument (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --exec-path, --super-prefix, --config-env), whose value is now its own token, are skipped so the value is not misread as the subcommand. The BARE message body is deliberately NOT matched against the identity set: a legitimate message that merely mentions an AI product name (-m "fix claude adapter") records no AI identity, and denying it would be a false positive; only a trailer or an --author value records identity. On a shell parse error (unbalanced quotes) it fails SAFE: a conservative raw-string scan denies an apparent AI trailer/--author/env/config assignment, never a silent-allow. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the common/accidental case (the assistant own accidental violation), not an adversary determined to evade it. It does NOT defeat deliberate shell escaping (git \commit), obfuscation, an alias or function that renames the tool, or persistent shell/env/config state such as an AI identity persisted in git config in a PRIOR TURN (not the same command), a trailer staged into a message file and committed with -F/-t, a commit made outside the Bash tool or the session, or an AI product name outside the recognized identity set.

SessionStart cannot block at the platform (exit 2 shows stderr only, doc-confirmed 2026-08-29), so this layer SURFACES divergence and ARMS the PreToolUse resume barrier; the barrier is the mechanism. Probes, all fail-closed to a finding rather than a silent pass: the declared handoff's Branch line against the real HEAD (scrubbed read-only probe), a handoff gate marker's commit against the real HEAD commit, lease staleness, every declared record surface readable (a declared-but-unreadable surface is a cannot-evaluate FINDING, never nothing-to-check), and merge-pending rows against first-parent merge evidence. Registry-scoped; with no registry it is silent. It reads records and git state only; it cannot detect a handoff that is stale in ways its declared grammar does not carry (free-text drift), and lease MISMATCH detection is bounded to staleness because a session cannot prove its own identity against the holder field.

REGISTRY-SCOPED: entirely inert unless an orchestration registry (.aiqt/orchestration.local.json or .aiqt/orchestration.json) is present AND a declared orchestrator lease or mode record is live, so plain Q&A sessions and bounded workers never inherit the global backlog. FAIL-OPEN by design on the stop path: an unresolvable cwd, an unreadable registry, an unreadable turn-state, an enumerator error or timeout, and an unreadable lease all ALLOW the stop, with the failure surfaced as a finding in the warn banner and the guard-events log, never a wedge. The deny is BOUNDED: the guard's own persisted counter (turn-state, reset on genuine human input) allows at most two denies per epoch, then ALLOWS WITH FINDINGS, independent of any platform loop field (none is documented on Stop; a loop-ish payload field is honoured opportunistically if one ever appears). Blocker proofs are validated against their sources (the dispatch ledger, the pending-decisions surface, evidence freshness, the clock), but plausibly FABRICATED external evidence is not mechanically closable at this layer; the human-decision class proves only that a pending-decision row exists, never that the item genuinely crosses the human-oversight threshold, which stays human judgement. A best-effort QUOTE-AWARE LEXICAL check over the Bash command string: it is tokenized with a shell lexer (shlex, posix, punctuation-aware) that respects quotes and yields the shell operators ; | || && & ( ) as distinct tokens only when unquoted, then grouped into segments on those operators and on newlines, so a bare or subshell-grouped diff (git diff, ( git diff )) is caught even when chained after an allowed segment, and a separator inside a quoted argument no longer mis-splits. On a segment whose command word is git it denies a diff-producing subcommand: diff, show, and range-diff always; log, diff-tree, diff-index, diff-files with a patch flag (-p/-u/--patch); format-patch with --stdout; stash with a show subcommand and a patch flag. git global options that take an argument (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --exec-path, --super-prefix, --config-env), whose value is now its own token, are skipped so the value is not misread as the subcommand, and a leading inline env-assignment prefix (GIT_PAGER=cat git diff) is skipped so the command word still resolves to git. A diff-producer segment is ALLOWED in FOUR cases, each judged PER DIFF SEGMENT on that segment own tokens: (1) an INFO FLAG on the segment (--help or -h) is a help invocation, not a diff; (2) a SUMMARY flag (--stat, --name-only, --name-status, --numstat, --shortstat) with NO co-present patch flag (-p, -u, --patch, --patch-with-stat, --patch-with-raw), so a listing form escapes but git diff --stat -p (which still dumps the full diff) DENIES; (3) the segment LAST stdout redirect targets a REAL non-console file (a > or >> token whose target is an ordinary path). Last-redirect-wins: a segment may carry more than one stdout redirect and only the last one governs where stdout finally lands, so git diff >/dev/tty >/tmp/x diverts to a real file (allow) while git diff >/tmp/x >/dev/tty ends on the console (deny). (4) a PAGER PIPE, the segment piped by an unquoted | into a known interactive pager (less, more, most, pager), is interactive review, not a console wall. Cases 1 and 4 (--help/-h and the pager pipe) were restored in GD-24 fix round 7 after fix round 6 over-corrected them to DENY; a pipe to cat, tee, or anything else is NOT a pager pipe and still denies. A redirect whose winning target lands on a console/terminal or on stdout/stderr is NOT an escape, because the diff still reaches the console: ANY target under /dev/ (/dev/tty, /dev/pts/N, /dev/console, /dev/stdout, /dev/stderr, any /dev/fd/N) or under /proc/ (/proc/self/fd/1, any /proc/PID/fd/N), and the fd-duplication forms (>&1, >&2, 1>&2, 2>&1, &>, >&), which tokenize as their own >&/&> tokens and are never a stdout-to-file redirect (a stdout fd-dup as the last redirect also keeps the segment a console dump). There is NO comment escape: the fragile # allow-diff quote-parsing was removed in GD-24 fix round 6 and stays removed (an opt-in anti-diff-dump hook blocks console diffs, and the summary and file-redirect escapes cover the legitimate want-the-diff-not-as-a-wall case). On a shell parse error (unbalanced quotes) it fails SAFE: a conservative raw-string scan denies an apparent git diff-producer with no summary or redirect-to-file escape, never a silent-allow. It does NOT defeat deliberate shell escaping (git \diff), obfuscation or indirection (printf, octal, eval, base64), an alias or function that renames the tool, persistent shell/env/config state or a prior-state (a pager or config set in an EARLIER turn), the env VAR=x git ... command form (the literal env command) or the command git ... builtin, a diff produced by a non-git tool or assembled across commands, a file written then dumped with cat, or a diff emitted outside the Bash tool. Two exotic escapes are ACCEPTED, not fixed (neither is reachable by accidental assistant behaviour): a pathspec LITERALLY named --help after a -- separator (git diff -- --help dumps a file named --help, but the info-flag escape matches the --help token without distinguishing option position from pathspec position, so it allows); and a pager whose OWN output is piped onward (the pager-pipe escape confirms the next command word is a pager but does not follow what happens after it, so a pager feeding a further console dump still escapes). It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the common/accidental case (the assistant own accidental violation), not an adversary determined to evade it.

This Stop layer is a NON-BLOCKING surfacing WARN (systemMessage, exit 0), not a hard block: by Stop time the wall has already rendered, and with no stop_hook_active field and no documented loop bound a hard block could wedge the session, so hard prevention lives in the PreToolUse diff-source layer instead. It catches only a unified-diff wall in the final assistant message of a turn: diff --git headers, paired @@ hunk headers, fenced diff/patch/udiff blocks (backtick or tilde) of 10 or more lines, and mixed +/- runs of 8 or more lines. It does not catch a diff dumped mid-turn between tool calls, side-by-side or word-diff renderings, or raw log or patch walls that carry none of those markers; a mixed +/- Markdown checklist can rarely trip the +/- run detector (accepted residual).

The TeammateIdle binding of the same decision core as orch-stop-guard, sharing its registry/lease scoping, escape, counter bound, and guard-events logging. A deny (exit 2) prevents the teammate from going idle past enumerated actionable work. On cannot-evaluate (enumerator error, unreadable registry or state) it takes the STOP branch, failing OPEN to allow the idle with findings, because forcing continued work on missing evidence could ping-pong a session; the plan's deny-on-cannot-evaluate applies only to the tool-mediated schedule path, where a denied call cannot wedge anything. Same disclosed bounds as orch-stop-guard on ledger blind spots and fabricated blocker evidence. Fires only where the platform emits TeammateIdle (doc-confirmed 2026-08-29); platforms without the event keep only the Stop and yield-tool bindings.

The scheduled-yield binding of the decision core: a call that parks the run (schedule_idle) or ends the loop (a ScheduleWakeup with stop=true is classified stop) is judged against a fresh enumeration. Registry-scoped and lease-scoped like orch-stop-guard; a tool the registry's yield_tools list does not name is out of scope even inside the matcher, and a registry yield tool OUTSIDE this fixed matcher is NOT covered (the doctor flags it; a manifest matcher is fixed at generation). On the schedule path a cannot-evaluate DENIES (missing evidence never licenses new autonomy; a denied tool call cannot wedge a session), bounded by a three-denial cap on an unchanged basis, after which it ALLOWS WITH FINDINGS so the guard cannot be farmed into bypass training. That cap needs persistable, readable turn-state; when the state directory is unreadable or unwritable the denial count cannot accumulate, so the schedule path stays fail-closed to DENY (the safe direction: the run keeps working rather than idling) and the cap does not relieve. Wake hygiene: a permitted schedule must name the tracked item or blocker it will recheck in its own text, judged by token containment (a paraphrase that names neither id nor ref denies once, a disclosed over-fire). The quiet-duration check is a best-effort regex: it fires only when the call text carries a parseable minutes claim AND turn-state carries a measured gap, and then the measured figure wins; an unparseable claim or an unknown measured endpoint authorizes nothing and is not invented. A fired timer or an existing cron is never counted as a live task or a blocker.

It never blocks. Classification is digest matching against wake registrations this suite itself recorded: a wake fired through a mechanism the suite never saw is stamped as genuine human input (the safe direction: it only narrows guard autonomy). A best-effort QUOTE-AWARE LEXICAL check over the Bash command string (the shipped shlex segmentation) with a SPLIT posture: the unambiguous git hook bypass DENIES; the two gate-shaped heuristics ASK, because "what is a gate" is not lexically certain. The DENY core: on a git segment whose subcommand accepts --no-verify (commit, merge, push, pull, rebase, am; the roster and the short-flag semantics verified against the git 2.53.0 man pages, 2026-08-19), a --no-verify spelling denies, matched exact or by CONSERVATIVE LONG PREFIX (an ambiguous abbreviation git itself would reject, such as --no-ver, is treated as the bypass anyway, and a separated option VALUE that itself spells --no-verify is scanned too - both safe-direction over-matches that only deny, never allow), and the SHORT -n denies ONLY on the two verbs where -n IS --no-verify (commit and am), clustered or bare, with the value-taking short and long options skipped so an option value carrying the letter n (an attached -m value, a separated --message value, a post -- pathspec) is never read as the flag; on push -n is --dry-run and on merge and pull it is --no-stat, so -n there is deliberately NOT flagged (flagging it would block safe dry runs), and --no-verify-signatures merely re-asserts a default and is not flagged. The ASK heuristics: a checker-shaped segment - a known checker command word (pytest, tox, nox, mypy, ruff, flake8, pylint, eslint, tsc, jest, mocha, rspec, shellcheck, gitleaks, pre-commit, ctest and kin), a command whose name PARTS (split on non-alphanumerics) contain test/check/lint/verify/validate/audit/selftest/conformance (run_all_checks.sh, selftest_aiqt_hooks.py; exact part match, so a word like "latest" never trips a substring), or a known runner (make, npm, yarn, pnpm, npx, go, cargo, mvn, gradle, python, bash and kin) invoking such an operand - whose failure is swallowed by an immediately following unquoted "|| true" or "|| :", or whose output is piped by an unquoted "|" into a truncating sink (head, tail) that under default pipeline semantics replaces the checker exit status with its own and can cut the failing output, ASKS. It does NOT catch: a gate weakened at its SOURCE (a workflow edited to carry continue-on-error or allow_failure, a deleted test, a lowered threshold - file-edit surfaces, not Bash commands); an environment-variable skip a hook manager honours (SKIP= for the pre-commit framework, HUSKY=0); hooks disabled by CONFIGURATION (core.hooksPath pointed at an empty directory, inline -c or persisted); an alias, wrapper, or shell function that renames git or the checker; a checker outside the lexicon whose name carries no checker-shaped part (an unknown gate roster is the honest bound of a lexical checker notion); a swallow spelled differently (|| exit 0, || echo, ; true, a set +e, a conditional wrapper); a truncating sink beyond head and tail (sed q, awk NR limits, grep -m); a script body inside sh -c quotes or an eval/xargs indirection (one opaque token to the lexer); a swallow separated from its checker by grouping parens (( pytest ) || true reads as adjacent to the paren, not the checker); pipefail state (under set -o pipefail a pipeline does keep the checker failure status, but shell state is invisible here, so a piped checker still ASKS - an accepted over-ask); a shell REDIRECTION before the git subcommand or before a checker command word (git >/dev/null commit --no-verify ; >/dev/null pytest || true) is not stripped and can slip, the same post-shlex lexical boundary shared with the protected-line guard and routed to the common enforcement-hook redesign; an embedded unquoted # in a token, which the shared shlex tokenization treats as a comment start, dropping the rest of the line so git commit -m ticket#123 --no-verify and pytest foo#bar || true slip, the same post-shlex shell-syntax boundary as that redirect handling, shared across the lexical hooks and routed to the common enforcement-hook tokenizer redesign; or any execution outside the Bash tool. A checker probe whose swallow is INTENTIONAL (a discovery run) and a non-gate command whose NAME merely looks checker-shaped (a test.sh that gates nothing) are accepted over-ASKS, the disclosed scoping cost of the heuristic; a gate-shaped command the lexicon does not name is the matching under-coverage, both stated rather than hidden. Two further safe-direction over-blocks are disclosed, both contrived and non-bypassing: a trailing --verify that cancels an earlier --no-verify (git models the pair as a boolean where the last wins, so git commit --no-verify --verify does NOT bypass hooks, yet this presence test is order-insensitive and DENIES it), and a clustered -h help flag (git commit -hn ..., where git prints help and does not commit, but the short scan reads the clustered n as the bypass and DENIES); re-issue without the contrived flag combination. On a shell parse error it fails SAFE with conservative raw probes (git plus a no-verify verb plus a --no-ver spelling DENIES; git commit or am plus a short -n cluster ASKS, since the raw string cannot bind the cluster to its subcommand; a checker keyword plus a raw "|| true", "|| :", "| head", or "| tail" ASKS), which OVER-MATCH by design: prose naming the keywords, a --no-verbose, or an unrelated -n cluster can deny or ask an unparseable command that was safe - re-issue it parseable. Overlap with shipped controls is compatible, not duplicated: a git push --no-verify --force to a protected branch is denied by BOTH this control and protected-line-guard, a git commit --no-verify on a protected HEAD denies here while protected-line-guard asks (deny outranks at the platform), and no other shipped control covers --no-verify, "|| true", or a truncating pipe on a non-diff command (the diff-source truncation reasoning governs diff producers only). It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the accidental case, not an adversary determined to evade it.

An ULTRA-CONSERVATIVE "ask unless PRISTINE and provably clean" guard (EN-6; supersedes the GD-41 coarse cut and the EN-4 fail-open-lexical hook) with THREE outcomes: ALLOW (exit 0 silent), ASK (permissionDecision ask, prompts the human), and DENY (permissionDecision deny, blocks). The `default` is "ask" because the recoverable ask is the characteristic behaviour; a confirmed whole-tree loss on a probed-dirty tree DENIES (unless the leading opt-out is set), BUT under a non-cosmetic ambient GIT_* var (an unresolvable repository view) even a whole-tree clobber ASKS with a best-effort cwd snapshot instead, because the guard cannot prove the target IS the session tree. It fails open (ALLOW) ONLY at the true boundary - a command with no git command-word, no recognized lossy verb, or an unparseable command (shlex ValueError) that names no lossy verb keyword - because that is not a discard it can reason about. WITHIN scope (a recognized lossy verb: checkout/switch/restore/reset/clean/stash/rm/branch) the outcome is ASK UNLESS the command is a PRISTINE SINGLE BARE `git <verb>` invocation AND (for a lossy form) the whole working tree is PROVABLY CLEAN, or the LEADING opt-out is set, or the form is genuinely non-destructive, in which cases ALLOW. PRISTINE SINGLE BARE is judged PURELY LEXICALLY (the bash grammar is NEVER parsed): after optional leading KEY=value assignments the command is exactly `git <args>` as ONE simple command, and the RAW string carries NO shell metacharacter ANYWHERE, EVEN INSIDE QUOTES - none of `;` `|` `&` `<` `>` `(` `)` `{` `}` `$` backtick backslash `!` newline, which by construction also rules out `&&`/`||`/`|&`, EVERY redirection form (`>`, `>>`, `<`, `2>`, `&>`, `>&`, `n>&m`, a leading or interspersed redirect), and EVERY command/process substitution (backtick, `$( )`, `<( )`, `>( )`) - AND no shell reserved word (if/then/elif/else/fi/for/while/until/do/done/case/esac/function/select/`[[`/`]]`/`{`/`}`) AND a command word that is LITERALLY `git` (not a path like /usr/bin/git, and not a wrapper: command/exec/builtin/env/xargs/time/`!`/sudo/nice/timeout/nohup/sh -c/bash -c). ANY shell metacharacter, wrapper, redirect, reserved word, second command, or option the classifier cannot resolve makes the command not-pristine, and it ASKS WITHOUT consulting the probe (a deliberate safe over-ask): treating the mere presence of shell structure in a lossy-verb command as an ASK is how the guard avoids modelling shell semantics it cannot model soundly. Only a metacharacter-free `git <verb> <plain args>` reaches the probe. PROVABLY CLEAN means the ONE read-only probe - `git -c status.showUntrackedFiles=all status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` (config-forced so a repo-local status.showUntrackedFiles=no CANNOT hide an untracked file, 5s timeout, offline) - reports NO tracked change (staged or unstaged, either column) AND NO untracked (`??`) entry; an untracked file is uncommitted work a force-checkout/clean/reset can destroy, so it counts as DIRTY (only an ignored `!!` entry is treated as clean). When a pristine bare lossy form is on a provably-clean tree it ALLOWs (nothing the probe can see to lose); a pristine bare WHOLE-TREE-clobbering verb (reset --hard by effective last-wins mode, checkout -f with no pathspec, switch --force/--discard-changes) on a probed-DIRTY tree DENIES (unless the leading opt-out is set; the reason wording covers untracked-only-dirty too); everything else in scope ASKS (unless the leading opt-out is set on a pristine bare form). There is NO claim that any compound, wrapped, redirected, or non-pristine form the guard RECOGNIZES as in-scope is proven safe: those are never ALLOWED, only ASKED (a pristine bare form carrying the leading opt-out is the sole override, short-circuiting even the redirect gate); the one exception is a wrapper that fragments the command word `git` or the verb so no recognized lossy verb is seen (a disclosed residual below), which reads as out-of-scope and is silently ALLOWED, not ASKED. A dirty tree ALONE does not force that outcome on a PRISTINE bare form: a dirty-tree WHOLE-TREE clobber DENIES and other non-pristine or redirected forms ASK, but a genuinely non-destructive form (reset --soft, plain switch, checkout -b, clean -n) can still ALLOW on a dirty tree when no redirect, opt-out, or ambient override applies. Verb forms (each ALLOWs only as a pristine bare command on a provably-clean tree, or one carrying the leading opt-out, except the unconditional-allow and unconditional-ask forms noted): checkout - a plain unforced branch-create (-b/--orphan) with NO merge option is an unconditional allow (git carries changes and aborts on conflict), and the NEW-BRANCH NAME argument of -b/-B (attached -bfoo or separated -b foo) is parsed as that name, never char-scanned as clustered force flags, so -bfoo/-bBranch ALLOW and are never mis-read as carrying -f/-B (F-85); -B is a force branch-create/RESET that overwrites an existing branch ref and can orphan committed commits, so it ASKS (including when combined with other flags); a -m/--merge or --conflict[=<style>] merge-switch, WITH or WITHOUT a -b create, does a three-way merge that can overwrite local changes and is worktree-scoped, decided before the branch-create allow (F-88); -p/--patch, any pathspec/bare-operand form, or a forced -f -b branch-create is worktree-scoped; -f with no pathspec is a whole-tree clobber. switch - -f/--force/--discard-changes is a clobber; -C/--force-create is a force branch-create/RESET that overwrites an existing branch ref and can orphan committed commits, so it ASKS; --merge/-m and --conflict[=<style>] are worktree-scoped (a three-way merge can overwrite local changes); a plain switch or an unforced -c create with NO merge option preserves non-conflicting local changes and aborts rather than lose them, so it is an unconditional allow, and the NEW-BRANCH NAME argument of -c/-C (attached -cfoo or separated -c foo) is parsed as that name, never char-scanned as clustered force flags, so -cfeature ALLOWs and is never mis-read as carrying -f/-C (F-85). restore - EVERY form is worktree-scoped, including --staged (it can erase staged-only content). reset - effective --hard clobbers; --soft is an unconditional allow (HEAD-only, index and worktree intact); --merge/--mixed/--keep/path-scoped/no-mode are scoped (index-changing); an ambiguous bare --m is scoped. rm - EVERY form is worktree-scoped, including --cached. clean - ANY non-dry-run clean is an unconditional ASK (untracked files are a different, unrecoverable asset, and the guard does not model whether the clean would fire, closing the clean.requireForce/-q/-i/clustered-flag edges); a -n/--dry-run judged before any `--` allows, BUT when an arg-consuming option -e/--exclude is present the `-n` is not trusted (it may be the exclude pattern) so the clean routes to its ASK. Destructive options are matched by CONSERVATIVE PREFIX (--patc=--patch, --del=--delete, --dis=--discard-changes, --har=--hard, --mer=--merge are unambiguous abbreviations git accepts; an AMBIGUOUS force-prefix like --for, which git itself REJECTS for branch as ambiguous with --format and for switch as ambiguous with --force-create, is treated as force ANYWAY, erring safe rather than recognizing only spellings git would accept); a `--`/`--end-of-options` boundary is respected so an operand after it (git clean -f -- -nasty, git rm -f -- --cached) is a pathspec, never a safe-looking option. stash drop/clear ASK, and stash export ASK for every spelling (F-95: export writes stash state to a ref, and --to-ref overwrites an arbitrary ref unconditionally); branch force forms ASK - -D/--delete --force (force delete), -M/--move --force (force rename), -C/--copy --force (force copy), -f/--force with an operand (force reset), and a delete (-d/-D/--delete) combined with -r/--remotes (F-94: deleting remote-tracking refs, which git force-removes past the merged-branch safeguard) - while a plain create/list, a local non-remotes -d, and an unforced -m/-c stay allow, and an attached -u<upstream> value (-ufoo, -u <upstream>) is parsed as the upstream, never scanned as a clustered force flag. A `git -C <dir> ...` or a GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE-prefixed form is pristine-lexically but names a worktree the guard cannot resolve to the session cwd, so it ASKS (unless the leading opt-out is set, evaluated before this redirect gate) rather than trust a session-dir probe. An AMBIENT GIT_*-prefixed var in the process env also forces ASK unless it is one of a small COSMETIC allowlist (UI/editor/pager/prompt/lock/identity vars that cannot change the discard target, the object/ref view, the index, or dirtiness detection): the probe scrubs every ambient GIT_* and reads the real cwd repo, but the guard cannot scrub them from the ACTUAL command, which still inherits them and may act on a different git dir, work tree, index, or object/ref view, so the guard cannot prove the repository view the ACTUAL command uses IS the session cwd. Under any such non-cosmetic ambient var EVERY in-scope pristine form ASKS (unless the leading opt-out is set, which is evaluated even earlier and short-circuits this gate) - a destructive clobber AND an otherwise-non-destructive allow form (reset --soft, plain switch, clean -n, checkout -b) alike, checked BEFORE the role/allow logic - each with a best-effort cwd snapshot WHEN the session cwd is a not-provably-clean snappable tree (no usable session cwd, a provably-clean cwd, or a stash/branch-only form, takes none; the snapshot may not capture a redirected tree), so no allow form and no clean cwd probe wins a silent ALLOW under such a redirect. A GIT_TRACE* var is NOT cosmetic: an absolute GIT_TRACE value makes the ACTUAL command append trace output to that path (which could be a repo file), so it too forces ASK, unless the leading opt-out is set (the recovery/probe git calls still scrub the whole GIT_TRACE family per round 6, so THEY write no trace, but the ambient GIT_TRACE on the command itself is not neutralized). This is FAIL-SAFE by construction rather than a fixed enumeration (which kept missing new members - GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS, GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE, GIT_REFERENCE_BACKEND - and more will exist): an unknown or new non-cosmetic GIT_* var ASKS rather than winning a silent ALLOW. This control is SIDE-EFFECTING (EN-6 recovery layer): before it ALLOWS or ASKS a snapshottable in-scope discard (checkout/switch/restore/reset/rm/clean) whose worktree it can resolve to the session cwd AND whose tree is NOT provably clean, it takes an INERT recovery snapshot of the uncommitted work and appends one line to an EXTERNAL per-user ledger, so a discard that is asked-then-approved OR wrongly allowed by a mis-parse is still recoverable (the hook fires once, with no post-approval callback). F-D EXPANSION: a NON-PRISTINE in-scope ASK (a compound, wrapped, or redirected snapshottable command) is ALSO snapshot-backed BEST-EFFORT against the SESSION CWD repo, so an asked-then-approved wrapped discard is recoverable too; because the redirected dir of a non-pristine command is NOT parsed, a command that changes into a DIFFERENT repository may be snapshotted at the session repo rather than the target (a same-repo cd is still captured by the whole-tree `git add --all`), and on snapshot fail the decision stays ASK. The snapshot uses a TEMPORARY GIT_INDEX_FILE outside the repo (seeded by copying the real index), `git add --all` (captures tracked-modified + UNTRACKED; ignored excluded), `git write-tree`, `git commit-tree` (parent = HEAD when present), and a CREATE-ONLY `git update-ref refs/aiqt-recovery/<utc-ts>-<pid> <sha>` with an empty expected-old value (a name collision FAILS the snapshot rather than clobbering a prior recovery ref). The snapshot writes only git objects and one private ref (plus a reflog entry for it when core.logAllRefUpdates=always, or when a reflog already exists for the ref) and does NOT itself touch the real index, worktree, HEAD, or any branch; the ref is invisible to plain `git status`, `git branch`, and `git log` but is reachable via `git log --all` / `git for-each-ref refs/aiqt-recovery` / `git show-ref` (a real ref, not hidden). Every real-state git call in this control takes an ALLOWLIST posture, scrubbing EVERY ambient GIT_*-prefixed var rather than enumerating a family (rounds 4-5 kept finding new members: GIT_CONFIG_*, then GIT_TRACE*, then GIT_ATTR_SOURCE), so an ambient decoy repo (GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE), an ambient `git -c` (GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS) config injection, an ambient GIT_ATTR_SOURCE attribute-source redirect, or an ambient GIT_TRACE that would make a read-only call WRITE a trace file cannot reach these calls; the scrub itself re-asserts GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (so the scrub cannot strip the offline + non-interactive posture: no partial-clone lazy-fetch over the network, no prompting) plus a FIXED INTERNAL recovery identity (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=aiqt-recovery, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=aiqt-recovery@localhost) so the snapshot `git commit-tree` never depends on an ambient or on-disk user.name/user.email the scrub removed - which would make it FAIL where no git identity is configured (a CI runner or fresh install with no global gitconfig), silently disabling the recovery backstop - and a recovery commit is deterministically attributed to the guard, not the user, the callers re-apply only the few vars they set themselves AFTER the scrub (GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS for the read-only probe, a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE for a snapshot), and any GIT_* the call genuinely needed but was scrubbed fails SAFE to a probe/snapshot failure (fail-to-ASK, never a silent allow). This closes the whole ambient-env class at once; the residual is NOT limited to on-disk config - it spans the non-GIT_ environment (HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME/PATH/TMPDIR), on-disk git configuration AND attributes (repo/global/system .gitconfig and .gitattributes), index and ignore state, submodules and embedded repos, configured hooks and filters, PATH-based git resolution, and partial-clone object availability, all read by git by design. RESIDUAL (the honest bound on "inert"): the inert guarantee is BOUNDED, not categorical, because git may ADDITIONALLY run a git-configured (repo, global, system, or command-scope) program during the snapshot whose effect is outside this guard control - a clean/process filter runs on `git add --all` (the CHECK-IN / clean direction, NOT smudge, which would run only on a restore/checkout), an fsmonitor hook runs on the `git status` probe, and a reference-transaction hook plus a post-index-change hook can run on the temp-index write and on the `git update-ref`; a clean filter can TRANSFORM the captured bytes, so the snapshot is NOT guaranteed byte-exact on a filtered repo; and a single overlaid tree cannot capture dirty content inside a SUBMODULE or an untracked EMBEDDED git repo (it stores only the gitlink) and flattens staged-vs-unstaged into ONE tree. The ledger is `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/aiqt-guardrails/recovery.jsonl` (normally outside the repo, so a `git clean` cannot destroy it). The ledger write is BEST-EFFORT: normally one line per snapshot, but skipped when no per-user location resolves (absent HOME/XDG), when that path would resolve inside the repo, or when the directory or write fails. A written line records: utc ts, repo path, the triggering git VERB (never the raw command or file contents), the recovery ref, the snapshot sha, the covered classes (tracked/staged/untracked), and the exact restore command (`git checkout <ref> -- :/`, OVERLAY mode: it brings back modified and new content but does NOT re-apply a recorded file deletion; for an exact, deletion-inclusive restore use an isolated branch via `git switch -c aiqt-recover-<id> <ref>`). The snapshot is decision-INDEPENDENT (it does not trust the form-classifier), so it also fires on a genuinely-safe snapshottable form (reset --soft, plain switch, checkout -b, clean -n) on a dirty tree, an accepted over-snapshot; it is SKIPPED on a provably-clean tree, out of scope, and for stash/branch (a worktree snapshot cannot capture stash entries or branch commits). FAIL POSTURE: when a warranted snapshot cannot be made (probe/write error, an undecodable non-UTF-8 path, over a ~100 MiB changed-content size cap, a bare or broken git dir, or a temp dir resolving inside the repo) it NEVER becomes a silent allow of a not-provably-clean discard - a would-be ALLOW is DOWNGRADED to ASK ("no recovery point could be created"), and an already-ASK/DENY decision is left as-is with the failure surfaced. Retention is NOT handled here (refs accumulate; auto-pruning is a separate maintenance op, never inside PreToolUse). An explicit GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD truthy assignment (anything but "", "0", "false", "no", "off"; an empty final assignment `GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD=` is falsy by bash last-wins and does NOT opt out) LEADING a pristine bare git command (the documented `GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD=1 git ...` prefix, not the same string buried in an argument nor on a non-pristine/compound command) opts out to ALLOW: being an explicit override in which the operator takes full responsibility, it is evaluated FIRST and short-circuits ALL of the gates below for that pristine form - the command-local-redirect/ambient view-uncertainty gate, the dirty-tree DENY, and the recovery layer alike - so an opt-out discard is NOT snapshot-backed, and a non-pristine form is never rescued by it (the opt-out is honoured only on a pristine single bare command). On an UNPARSEABLE command (shlex ValueError) the opt-out is NOT honoured at all: the guard cannot parse the command, so it cannot soundly trust an opt-out-looking prefix inside it, and an unparseable in-scope command ALWAYS ASKS. HONEST RESIDUAL: being a LEXICAL hook it does NOT catch a git alias (config-defined; an inline `-c alias.<name>=...` now ASKS) or shell function that renames git or expands to a work-losing verb, a discard performed OUTSIDE the Bash tool, or persistent shell/config state set in a PRIOR turn. It also does NOT catch a real discard whose VERB is OUTSIDE the recognized set AND unflagged by the raw scan: a `git worktree remove -f` (or `--force`) of a dirty linked worktree discards the uncommitted work in that worktree, but `worktree` matches no lossy keyword, so the command is allowed at the true boundary; that verb is deliberately NOT added this round (disclosure matches the best-effort posture). By contrast (F-97), a command the raw scan DOES flag as in-scope whose resolved subcommand is nonetheless outside the recognized set (`git checkout-index -a -f`, `git read-tree -u --reset HEAD`, flagged by their `checkout`/`reset` substring) is NO LONGER silently allowed - it ASKS, since a flagged sub the classifier cannot resolve to a known verb cannot be proven non-destructive, and its sub is not snapshottable so no recovery point exists. It also does NOT catch deliberate token fragmentation or obfuscation of the COMMAND WORD `git` ITSELF or of the verb: a wrapper whose git command word or verb is SPLIT by shell quoting so neither the token scan nor the raw scan sees a contiguous git+work-losing keyword (a wrapped, quote-fragmented reset such as env git followed by a quote-broken re-set, or a command word quote-broken so it spells git only after the shell strips the quotes (a quote-broken git under a wrapper such as command or env), whose raw string carries no contiguous `git`+`reset`) reads as "no recognized lossy verb" and is silently ALLOWED, so the claim that any wrapper ASKS is NOT categorical: it holds only while the raw scan still sees a contiguous git+verb keyword. This is a disclosed best-effort residual, not chased (the guard targets the accidental case, not an adversary deliberately splitting the command word or the verb). The probe ITSELF can be made to under-report dirtiness by git config or index state: an `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` mark on a tracked file, or a `submodule.<name>.ignore` setting, hides real modifications from `git status`, so the guard can read a genuinely-dirty tree as provably clean and ALLOW a discard of that hidden work; and the recovery snapshot ALSO cannot capture assume-unchanged/skip-worktree content (it is not in what `git add --all` re-stages) nor IGNORED files (git add --all excludes them; an ignored file overwritten by a forced checkout or removed by `clean -x` is unprobed - to avoid asking on every repo carrying build artifacts - and unsnapshotted). Beyond that, being ultra-conservative it OVER-ASKS heavily - every compound, wrapped, redirected, or metacharacter-bearing command that names a lossy verb ASKS even when it would have been safe (a pristine bare form carrying the leading opt-out is the sole override, short-circuiting even the redirect gate), and a command that merely CONTAINS a git token and a lossy verb as TEXT while running no discard (`echo git branch`, `git log | grep branch`) ASKS too, because the raw scan matches the keywords wherever they appear (a safe-direction over-ask, not narrowed: narrowing the raw scan is the whack-a-mole GD-34 rejected), and a pristine whole-tree clobber over-DENIES on a dirty tree even when the specific target would have lost nothing - an accepted, recoverable cost of never silently allowing a real WORKING-TREE-CONTENT discard for a recognized command that is NOT covered by the explicit leading opt-out or a disclosed residual. That no-silent-allow guarantee is bounded to working-tree content: ref-level moves (reset --soft moving HEAD, a merged-branch delete) are reflog-recoverable, and the obfuscation/config residuals above are best-effort, not categorical.

A best-effort QUOTE-AWARE LEXICAL check over the Bash command string (the shipped shlex segmentation): it judges git push and git commit segments only - the LITERAL commit subcommand; a merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, or rebase that also lands commits on the protected line is out of scope by design, because the accidental case this layer guards is the direct git commit and server-side branch protection remains the real gate. The push layer parses options with a value-skip for the separated value-taking options (--push-option/-o, --repo, --receive-pack/--exec, and --recurse-submodules, whose value is MANDATORY and hence separable - verified against git 2.53.0, which consumes the next token as the value and rejects a bare form) and a --/--end-of-options boundary. Force, delete, sweep, and prune flags are detected VALUE-AWARE inside the token loop, so an option value is never read as a flag (git push -o --force origin main carries a push-option VALUE, not a force flag): every force spelling counts (-f/--force clustered or long, any --force-with-lease spelling - a lease-guarded force still rewrites the remote ref - --force-if-includes, and --mirror, which implies force), plus the ref-sweeping modes: --mirror, a forced --all/--branches, the MATCHING refspec (a bare : pushes every branch existing on both ends and +: is its forced form; either ASKS, a matching-refspec push this guard cannot prove misses the protected branches), and --prune combined with a wildcard or matching refspec (which DELETES every remote branch absent locally with NO force flag - witnessed deleting a remote master - so it ASKS; a --prune whose refspec mapping comes only from configuration falls under the configuration residual below). Operand ROLES follow the grammar git itself uses (git push <repository> <refspec>...): the FIRST bare operand is the repository and is never judged as a destination (a remote literally named main is not a false deny), and only the later, refspec-position operands are judged, by exact case-sensitive DESTINATION name (tolerant of a refs/heads/ or heads/ prefix); a skip-set omission can only shift operands toward over-inclusion, never move a real refspec into the exempt repository slot. A protected DELETION is denied like a force: a --delete or clustered -d flag whose refspec-position operand names a protected branch, and the empty-source :<dst> delete refspec (:main); the deny banner names the actual act, force-push vs branch deletion. When no refspec names a destination (a refspec-less force-push) or the refspec is HEAD/@, the SESSION-CWD current branch is read by a scrubbed read-only symbolic-ref probe (every ambient GIT_* removed, offline, 5s timeout), and a detached or unreadable HEAD reads as UNKNOWN, never as not-protected. Git resolves a pushed or FORCED HEAD/@ to the current branch; a DELETED HEAD or :@ git itself REJECTS as a nonexistent or invalid remote ref, so the probe-backed deny on a deleted HEAD/@ is a harmless safe-direction over-deny kept for uniformity, not a claim that git resolves a deleted HEAD to the current branch. It does NOT catch: a push or commit outside the Bash tool; a git alias or shell function that renames git or expands to a push; a destination supplied by SHELL EXPANSION rather than a literal token (git push --force origin "$BRANCH" with BRANCH holding a protected name, a command substitution, or a glob): a lexical guard judges the literal token and cannot resolve runtime shell state - the same inherent boundary git_discard discloses for its variable and substitution forms; a FRAGMENTED command word or verb (shell quoting that splits the git command word or the push/commit verb so neither the parsed segments nor the raw scan sees a contiguous git-plus-verb keyword; a plain command-word wrapper such as env/sudo/command/xargs IS caught by the raw scan and ASKS); a WRAPPED push in a compound in which ANY other segment, EARLIER OR LATER, parses with git as its command word (git status && sudo git push --force origin main, and equally env git push --force origin main && git status): the benign git segment satisfies the saw-git check, so the wrapped-catch raw scan never runs and the wrapped force-push is silently allowed - an adversarial best-effort residual of the same class as the fragmented command word, disclosed and not chased; a destination supplied by CONFIGURATION rather than the command line (push.default, branch.<name>.pushRemote/merge, remote.<name>.push refspecs, a triangular-push setup), so the bare-push HEAD proxy can diverge from the configured upstream mapping; a protected line under a NON-DEFAULT name (the set ships as main/master); or a rewrite landed on the remote side or by a hosting-provider action (a protected-NAMED force-push or deletion is denied redirect-independently, and a current-branch force-push or deletion under an unresolvable -C/--git-dir/GIT_* redirect ASKS, so none silent-allows). SAFE-DIRECTION OVER-DENIES, accepted and disclosed (re-issue without the contrived flag combination): negation and no-op flags are not modelled, so a --force or --delete cancelled by a later --no-force/--no-delete still denies, --force-if-includes ALONE (a documented no-op without --force-with-lease) denies, and a --dry-run push carrying any force or delete spelling is judged like the real thing and denies. On a shell parse error, OR when a command-word wrapper hides git so no parsed segment resolves to git, it falls back to a conservative raw scan that ASKS (never a hard deny, never a silent allow) on an apparent git force-push (any -f/--force/--for-prefix/--mirror/--all form, or a +refspec anchored to start, whitespace, or either quote character, so a quoted "+main:main" under sudo is caught), an apparent branch deletion (a --de-prefix long flag, or a d carried ANYWHERE in a short - cluster, mirroring the force cluster shape so a wrapped -dv is caught, name-independent like the force spellings; or an empty-source :<protected-name> refspec, judged by its visible name), or an apparent git commit. The raw scan OVER-MATCHES by design (a case-different name, an attached -o value ending in f, an unrelated + or -d token, or prose mentioning the keywords ASKS), so re-issue a wrongly-flagged command as a plain, parseable git command. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the accidental case, not an adversary determined to evade it.

Registry-scoped: inert with no registry or no declared mode record. Blocks a blocking question ONLY when the declared operating-mode record contains 'unattended'; attended modes, an absent mode line, and an unreadable mode record all fail OPEN (this guards one known mistake shape, a blocking prompt idling an unattended run; it is not a security boundary), with the fail-open logged to guard-events. The deny instruction distinguishes record-and-continue for ordinary decisions from record-and-HOLD for anything at the human-oversight threshold; the hook redirects the question and never licenses acting without the answer. Each denied ask appends ONE idempotent machine row keyed on session_id plus tool_use_id, carrying a bounded redacted summary (question count, length, digest), never the question text. Its behaviour is verified by the behaviour self-test. It cannot see a blocking prompt raised outside the AskUserQuestion tool.

A RECORDING substrate, not an enforcement point: it appends launch rows (a Bash call with run_in_background true, or a registry-declared dispatch tool) and completion rows (a TaskOutput read) to the machine-written dispatch ledger the stop guard consumes as its Gap-B oracle. It never blocks; a failed ledger write is surfaced as a non-blocking systemMessage, never swallowed. Coverage is exactly the hooked tools: a launch through an unhooked tool is invisible (costing one spurious stop-guard deny), a completion that never passes through TaskOutput is invisible until the staleness horizon expires the row, and the task-id extraction from tool responses is best-effort field matching. Both blind-spot directions are bounded by staleness plus the resume audit, and disclosed at the stop guard.

gates.residue: Total over the surface it examines: an OPEN merge_pending row carrying a TYPED ref (pr:N, decision:X) whose merge or record evidence exists in the declared truth sources always fails the gate. It reads only typed structured refs; a narrative number in prose, an untyped row, or a register kept outside the declared surface is out of scope by design (D9), and drift the truth sources themselves cannot see (an unpushed local merge, a PR merged under a subject with no (#N) marker) passes. In a checkout with no orchestration registry the live leg is NOT APPLICABLE (the record is machine-local by design) and the self-test carries the assurance; that scope boundary is printed, never silent.

hooks.residue: SessionStart cannot block at the platform (exit 2 shows stderr only, doc-confirmed 2026-08-29), so this layer SURFACES divergence and ARMS the PreToolUse resume barrier; the barrier is the mechanism. Probes, all fail-closed to a finding rather than a silent pass: the declared handoff's Branch line against the real HEAD (scrubbed read-only probe), a handoff gate marker's commit against the real HEAD commit, lease staleness, every declared record surface readable (a declared-but-unreadable surface is a cannot-evaluate FINDING, never nothing-to-check), and merge-pending rows against first-parent merge evidence. Registry-scoped; with no registry it is silent. It reads records and git state only; it cannot detect a handoff that is stale in ways its declared grammar does not carry (free-text drift), and lease MISMATCH detection is bounded to staleness because a session cannot prove its own identity against the holder field.

The mutation barrier behind orch-resume-audit, shipped WARN-FIRST (stage bake, a recorded posture): while the barrier state is armed it surfaces a systemMessage on the first mutation outside the allowlist (the record surfaces, the registry files, and the suite's own state directory stay writable, so the only exit, correcting the record, is never blocked), and it blocks nothing during the bake. The flip to deny is a manifest edit (stage to enforce, default to ask/deny) taken on recorded guard-events evidence after the bake period, per the guardrail-config-integrity discipline. Bash targets are not path-judged (a command's write targets are not lexically resolvable), so Bash mutations pass with the same surfacing only. Clearing the barrier requires re-running the audit (tools/orch_doctor.py --resume-audit) against corrected records; acknowledgement alone does not clear it.

gates.residue: Total over the declared register: a broken digest chain or sequence, a reused id, an illegal status transition, a rewrite of anchored or merge-base rows, and an unverifiable landed row always fail; a declared-but-unreadable register is exit 2. A same-authority local file offers no protection against an actor who rewrites the WHOLE chain and the anchor together, which defeats the untracked mode (the tracked mode is bounded by merge-base history instead), so rewrites are DETECTABLE within those bounds, never prevented; adopters needing real separation bind the same interface to a server-side append store. The landed-row check proves the cited commit and check path exist, not that the check semantically guards the mistake. In a checkout with no registry the live leg is NOT APPLICABLE with the self-test as assurance.

A pattern scanner for hardcoded credentials: it catches recognizable provider-token prefixes and assignments of a literal to a credential-named variable. It misses a high-entropy string with no telltale name or prefix, an encoded secret, and a secret in a binary (the measured residue of 2026-08-08, shared with gitleaks). Detection here is a compensating control, never a substitute for keeping the secret out of the repository in the first place.

hooks.residue: A COMPENSATING control, not a replacement: the CI secret-scan and gitleaks gates remain the real backstop, and this layer moves the same high-signal detection to the moment a secret would be written, so an accidental paste is caught before it lands on disk rather than only at commit or CI time. It SINGLE-SOURCES its shapes from tools/check_secrets.py (the pack source of truth), rendered into the handler by tools/gen_secret_patterns.py and drift-gated so the two can never fork: the recognizable provider-token PREFIX shapes (GitHub, GitHub fine-grained PAT, OpenAI-style, OpenAI project key, Anthropic, AWS access key id, Slack, Slack app-level token, a private key block header) and the credential-named ASSIGN shape (a passwd/password/secret/token/api-key/access-key/client-secret/auth-token/private-key/credential variable assigned a literal of real length). It EXCLUDES obvious placeholders (the shared PLACEHOLDER shape: your/my/the-prefixed names, change-me, example, sample, dummy, redacted, fake, test, todo, none, null, n/a, an angle-bracket or dollar-brace or dollar-VAR template, and runs of x/dot/star), and for an UNQUOTED assignment value it additionally requires both a letter and a digit, exactly as check_secrets.py does, so ordinary prose does not trip it. It scans the content a Write would write, the new_string an Edit would introduce, the concatenation of the new_string values a MultiEdit would introduce across its edits, or the command string a Bash call would emit, and DENIES on a real match, naming only the pattern label and never echoing the secret value. DISCLOSED non-catches: an entropy-only secret with no recognizable prefix or credential-named assignment (the same gap check_secrets.py and gitleaks both disclose); a secret written by a tool other than Write, Edit, MultiEdit, or Bash (other content tools such as NotebookEdit are out of scope, routed to a periodic pattern review); a secret split across tokens or lines or assembled by concatenation, since the scan is per-line and lexical; on the Bash path the command string is scanned as RAW TEXT (it is not shlex-tokenized and is not executed), so a secret assembled by concatenation or supplied through a shell variable or expansion is missed, but a redirect or an embedded # does NOT cause a Bash-path miss (the raw-text scan carries no post-shlex boundary, so the earlier redirect / embedded-# disclosure was inaccurate and is corrected here); the ASSIGN shape also does not match a JSON-style quoted credential key ("api_key": "...") or a triple-quoted value, a curated-pattern-set format-completeness gap routed to the periodic pattern review (backlog L12) with gitleaks the exhaustive backstop; the curated-pattern-set completeness and tuning (the F-127 env-lookup false-positives and further provider-token variants) are out of scope and routed to that periodic pattern review, with gitleaks the exhaustive backstop; and a base64-encoded or otherwise obfuscated form. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the accidental paste or commit, not an adversary deliberately encoding or fragmenting a secret to evade it.

SessionStart cannot block at the platform (exit 2 shows stderr only, doc-confirmed 2026-08-29), so this layer SURFACES divergence and ARMS the PreToolUse resume barrier; the barrier is the mechanism.
